title: AKS Scaling and Day-2 Operations
description: Configure scaling in AKS with cluster autoscaler and HPA, and understand common day-2 operational tasks.

data.text: AKS supports two types of scaling: cluster autoscaler (adjusts the number of nodes) and Horizontal Pod Autoscaler (adjusts the number of Pod replicas). Together they provide full automatic scaling.
The cluster autoscaler monitors Pods that cannot be scheduled due to resource constraints. When it detects pending Pods, it adds nodes. When nodes are underutilized, it removes them.

data.title: Azure CLI - Enable Cluster Autoscaler
data.content:
# Create an AKS cluster with autoscaler enabled
az aks create \
  --resource-group myRG \
  --name myAKS \
  --node-count 3 \
  --enable-cluster-autoscaler \
  --min-count 1 \
  --max-count 10 \
  --generate-ssh-keys

# Update autoscaler bounds
az aks update --resource-group myRG --name myAKS \
  --update-cluster-autoscaler --min-count 2 --max-count 20

data.text: HPA automatically adjusts the number of Pod replicas based on CPU or memory utilization. It runs as a controller inside the Kubernetes cluster.

data.title: YAML - HorizontalPodAutoscaler
data.content:
apiVersion: autoscaling/v2
kind: HorizontalPodAutoscaler
metadata:
  name: myapp-hpa
spec:
  scaleTargetRef:
    apiVersion: apps/v1
    kind: Deployment
    name: myapp-deployment
  minReplicas: 2
  maxReplicas: 10
  metrics:
  - type: Resource
    resource:
      name: cpu
      target:
        type: Utilization
        averageUtilization: 70

data.title: Day-2 Operations
data.text: AKS day-2 operations include: upgrading Kubernetes versions, monitoring with Azure Monitor, backing up with Velero, scanning images with Microsoft Defender, and managing RBAC with Azure AD integration.

data.caption: Two-layer autoscaling in AKS
data.definition:
flowchart TB
    HPA[HPA: Pod Replicas] -->|Scale Out| P[More Pods]
    P -->|Not Enough Nodes?| CA[Cluster Autoscaler]
    CA -->|Add Node| N[New Node]
    N -->|Schedules Pods| P
    LOW[Low Utilization] -->|Scale In| CA
    CA -->|Remove Node| NR[Node Removed]

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: Cluster autoscaler adjusts the number of nodes
HPA adjusts the number of Pod replicas
Both work together for full horizontal scaling
Day-2 ops include upgrades, monitoring, and RBAC
data.takeaway: AKS auto-scaling operates at both the node and Pod levels for efficient resource usage.
